[RTCT.7.8] **Capability refusal is a load error.** An artefact whose rules can
reach a builtin that is not `rt_safe` ([IRET.13.3]) **must be refused at load**
under `realtime`, with `DS_ERR_RT_UNSAFE`. It must not be accepted and then
declined per-activation.

**Why the load and not the activation.** A realtime contract is a promise made
before the engine runs. An artefact accepted at load and refused mid-cycle has
already been promised for, and the integrator learns the promise was unkeepable
at the first fact that reaches the rule — which may be long after go-live and
is not reproducible from the artefact alone. Refusing at load makes the
contract checkable when it is offered.

**Which component performs the check is not specified here.** The compiler
knows every builtin a rule can reach and the loader holds the registration
table, so either can answer; what this clause fixes is that the answer arrives
**before any fact is processed**, and that the artefact is rejected rather than
degraded.

This is rung 1 of `[LERR.1]` — nothing is abandoned because nothing has
started. It is not a `TypeError`: a `TypeError` abandons one activation, and an
artefact that cannot honour `realtime` is not a per-activation condition.
